chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the blood money for a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian. He said: “They are equal: eight hundred, eight hundred.”

He said: I said, “May I be your ransom, if they are apprehended in the land of the Muslims while committing an indecent act, is the hadd punishment carried out upon them?” He said: “Yes, they are judged according to the rulings of the Muslims.”

key_terms.أَحْكَامِ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: the legal rulings of the Muslims
key_terms.ثَمَانُمِائَةٍ: eight hundred, the stated amount of diyyah
key_terms.دِيَةِ ٱلْيَهُودِيِّ: the blood money due for a Jewish person
key_terms.ٱلنَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian subject of the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْمَجُوسِيِّ: a Magian subject of the ruling

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the diyyah of Jews, Christians, and Magians, and about applying hadd penalties to them in Muslim lands?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the diyyah of a Jew, Christian, and Magian, stating that they are equal at eight hundred. It also states that if such persons are apprehended in Muslim lands committing a punishable indecency, they are judged according to the legal rulings applied by the Muslims.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5249 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Baṣir who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about the blood money (diyyah) for a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian.
Imam (as) replied: "They are equal - eight hundred (dirhams), eight hundred (dirhams)."

I asked: "May I be your ransom, if they are caught committing an immoral act in the land of the Muslims, is the legal punishment (hadd) applied to them?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes, they are judged according to the rulings of the Muslims."
